ruling: - **R36. Agents write little that no one reads.** Owner 12:49 CST Nov 11: "how much should our [agents] be allowed to just "type"". 12:52 CST: "im assuming the brief kinda needs to have a line in terms of how much to talk ... keep verbiage to a minimum something like that? or it's mechanized? unsure i'm deferring to you". Pick, under that deferral: the line goes in each agent role file and the lane start text, which load on their own, never in each brief. Briefs carry only task facts. A check proves each role file holds the line. Reasoning and tool inputs are never cut. The brief audit (started 12:48 CST) measures brief length and the narration share of lane output first; the line ships if narration is a real share. Measured 13:06 CST (read-only audit, scratchpad chatter-audit.md): narration plus final reply is 19-32% of visible output in standing sessions and 9% in a lane, so the line ships. It cuts context growth more than money: cache reads dominate cost. Each wake of an idle lane re-wrote about 200K tokens of cache for a short answer; that goes to 3.15. Owner 13:10 CST: "how to keep their prose from staying tight (maybe in their claude.md or mechanically idk or a judge that scans and says hey you yappin too much)". The reply judge gains one item: a reply longer than its reader needs, judged by who reads it, never by a word count (R37). It flags and never refuses. Home: agents/*.md; decisions agent-model-cap and reply-judge-samples-never-refuses.
